baslik: 4 patients die after Gaza Strip's only cancer hospital goes out of service
metin:
Four individuals passed away Thursday when the Turkish-Palestinian Friendship Hospital, Gaza's sole specialized cancer treatment facility, ceased operations.

Hospital director Subhi Skaik reported that "four cancer patients lost their lives today as a result of the Turkish Friendship Hospital stopping" due to fuel depletion. He explained the fatalities resulted from inadequate medical resources during the shutdown.

All remaining patients were relocated to Dar Al Salam Hospital in Khan Yunis, located in southern Gaza.

The facility halted services Wednesday following Israeli military strikes and fuel shortages. The UN's humanitarian coordination office noted that the hospital "ran out of fuel and was forced to stop its services," endangering approximately 70 cancer patients.

The incident occurred during an intensified Israeli military campaign against Gaza, which began following Hamas's October 7 cross-border offensive. The conflict has claimed nearly 10,600 lives—approximately 9,061 Palestinians and over 1,538 Israelis.

Gaza's 2.3 million residents face severe supply shortages due to the Israeli blockade, compounding the humanitarian crisis alongside mass casualties and displacement.
